values: archunit
<rule>

^(?!(?:spring-layout|spring-feature-boundary|spring-shared-pure|spring-controller-repository|spring-controller-entity|spring-service-web|spring-controller-controller|spring-repository-service|spring-scope-capture|ddd-aggregate-reference|ddd-foreign-entity|ddd-value-object-reference|spring-request-state|spring-test-placement|spring-no-dirties-context)$)
archunit/noCyclesBetweenFeatures
A rule of the project's own ArchUnit tests.
The project writes ArchUnit rules as tests named `*ArchTest` or `*ArchitectureTest`; nitpicker runs them and reports each violated rule by the name of its test field or method.
Fix the code the rule's message names.
ddd-aggregate-reference
A root or entity of one aggregate holds the root of another (`Customer customer` in `Order`); hold its identifier (`CustomerId`) or an `Association<Customer, CustomerId>`.

One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes: it keeps the package-by-feature layout, the layering and the aggregate boundaries that the TypeScript preset keeps with its import rules.

Refer to <OtherRoot> by its identifier or an Association<<OtherRoot>, ID> in <Class>: <OtherRoot> is the root of another aggregate, and holding it lets one aggregate change another outside its consistency boundary.
A module with jMolecules (`org.jmolecules:jmolecules-ddd`) on its main compile classpath, with or without Spring.
ddd-foreign-entity

A root or entity holds an entity that belongs to another aggregate (`List<CartLine>` in `Order` when `CartLine implements Entity<Cart, ...>`), or an `@Entity` that two roots reach (each root is reported, naming the other).
Refer to <Aggregate> by its identifier in <Class> instead of holding <Entity>: <Entity> belongs to the aggregate <Aggregate>, and an entity belongs to exactly one aggregate.
ddd-value-object-reference
A value object holds an aggregate root or an entity; hold its identifier.
Hold the identifier of <Entity> in <Class>, not the object: a value object is compared by its values, and <Entity> is an entity with an identity and lifecycle of its own.
spring-controller-controller

A controller holds or creates another controller: a field, constructor or method parameter of that type, also inside a generic, or `new OtherController()`. Naming another controller's class in a link (`methodOn(OrderController.class)`, a `Class<OrderController>`) is fine.
Move what <Class> needs from <OtherController> into a service both controllers call: a controller handles its own requests and does not hold another controller.
A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
spring-controller-entity

A request-mapping or `@ModelAttribute` method of a controller takes or returns an `@Entity` type, also inside a generic such as `List<Customer>`; methods declared on implemented interfaces (the OpenAPI-generator layout) and inherited from base controllers count.
Take and return a record (DTO) in <Class>.<method> and map it in the service: the entity <Entity> stays out of controller signatures.
spring-controller-repository

A `@Controller` or `@RestController` depends on a repository (`@Repository`, or a type extending Spring Data's `Repository`) or on data access directly (`JdbcTemplate`, `NamedParameterJdbcTemplate`, `JdbcClient`, `SimpleJdbcInsert`, R2DBC `DatabaseClient`, `JdbcAggregateTemplate`, `R2dbcEntityTemplate`, `MongoTemplate`, `EntityManager`, `EntityManagerFactory`, Hibernate `Session`, `DataSource`, or their interfaces), in a field, parameter, return type or call.
Have <Class> call a service that uses <Repository>: controllers call services only, not repositories or data access.
spring-feature-boundary
A class uses a class from a sub-package of another root package (`orders.internal.X` from `billing`); the classes directly in the other package are fine.
Have <Class> use only the classes directly in <root>.<feature>, or move what both need to <root>.shared: <OtherClass> is internal to that feature (<root>.<feature>.<package>).
spring-layout

A class sits directly in the root package (only `@SpringBootApplication`, `@Configuration` and `@ConfigurationProperties` classes and a `SpringBootServletInitializer` subclass may), or in a root sub-package named by layer: `controller(s)`, `service(s)`, `repository`/`repositories`, `entity`/`entities`, `model(s)`, `dto(s)`, `dao(s)`, `util(s)`, `common`, `web`, `api`, `rest`, `resource(s)`, `persistence`, `domain`, `mapper(s)`, `exception(s)`, `adapter(s)`, `application`, `infrastructure`, `infra`, `port(s)`, `usecase(s)`, `helper(s)`.

Put <Class> in the feature package it belongs to, <root>.<feature>, which holds that feature's controller, service and repository together (pure utilities go to <root>.shared); "<layer>" is a layer package.
spring-no-dirties-context
A test class or method has `@DirtiesContext`, anywhere.
Reset state in <Name>Test itself, or test the class without a Spring context: @DirtiesContext rebuilds the context and slows the suite.
spring-repository-service
A repository depends on a `@Service`: a field, parameter, return type or call. A repository depending on a controller or the web layer is `spring-service-web`.
Have the service call <Class> and pass it what it needs from <Service>: a repository only reads and writes data and depends on no service.
spring-request-state

Request data reaches a field of a singleton bean or a static field outside set-up: assigned, written into an array element, or passed to a collection, map, `Map.Entry` or `AtomicReference` mutator (`add`, `put`, `computeIfAbsent`, `set`, ...).

Pass the request data from <request source> on through parameters and return values instead of passing it to <Class>.<field> with <mutator>(): <Class> is a singleton that every request shares, so request data kept there leaks between users and races between threads. Per-request data belongs in a @RequestScope bean, and a cache needs a size and an expiry (Spring Cache, Caffeine).
spring-scope-capture

A singleton bean (a `@Component` class or a `@Bean` method without `@Scope`, or with `singleton` or `application` scope) takes a request-, session-, `websocket`-, Spring Batch `step`- or `job`-scoped bean without a scoped proxy: in a constructor or `@Bean` method parameter, an `@Autowired`, `@Inject` or `@Resource` field or method, also as `Optional<T>`, an array or a collection or map of them.

Inject ObjectProvider<<ScopedBean>> into <Class> and call getObject() per use, or give <ScopedBean> a scoped proxy (proxyMode = ScopedProxyMode.TARGET_CLASS): a singleton gets one <ScopedBean> when it is created, which fails outside a <scope> and otherwise keeps the first <scope>'s bean.
spring-service-web

A `@Service` or repository depends on the web layer: a controller or `@ControllerAdvice`, `ResponseEntity` in its own field, method or constructor signatures (not a `RestTemplate` or `RestClient` result it unwraps), or the `jakarta.servlet`, `javax.servlet`, `org.springframework.web.bind`, `org.springframework.web.servlet`, `org.springframework.web.multipart`, `org.springframework.web.context.request` (`RequestContextHolder`, `WebRequest`), `org.springframework.web.server` (`ServerWebExchange`, `ResponseStatusException`), `org.springframework.web.reactive` or `org.springframework.http.server` packages, so servlet and WebFlux apps are held to the same rule.
Keep <Class> free of web types: take and return plain values, throw a domain exception for errors, and map them to and from <WebType> in the controller or a @ControllerAdvice.
spring-shared-pure
A `shared` class is a Spring bean (`@Component` and its stereotypes, `@Configuration`) or an `@Entity`, or depends on a class in any other root package.
Move <Class> into the package that uses it, or drop its use of <OtherClass>: <root>.shared holds pure utilities and depends on no feature package such as <root>.<feature>.
spring-test-placement

Such a test is in the unit test source set (`test` on Gradle, the one test source directory on Maven) and is not an integration test by the shared rule of the [slow-test check](docs/java-preset.md#slow-tests): a class named `*IT`, `*ITCase`, `*IntegrationTest(s)`, `*IntegrationSpec` or `*ISpec`, or a package with an `integration`, `it` or `e2e` segment. The message offers the forms that keep the package (an `*IT` name, an integration test source set), so a slice test of a package-private controller still compiles; plain unit tests live anywhere.

Test <Name>Test with new and mocks, or run it as an integration test: name it <Name>IT (Failsafe runs *IT on Maven) or put it in an integration test source set. Both keep its package, so package-private classes stay visible; a package named integration or it also counts.
errorprone
InlineSuppression
An inline suppression of errorprone in a Java source.
A suppression annotation hides a finding from the report, so a source scan reports every one.
Do not silence Error Prone or NullAway inline: fix the finding (for NullAway, annotate what may be null with @Nullable).
google-java-format
format
A Java file is not formatted with google-java-format.
The Java presets keep one layout, the formatter's. google-java-format runs in check mode and reports every file it would change.

File is not formatted with google-java-format. Run nitpicker --fix, or format it with google-java-format --replace <Java files>. Not your formatter: pin "conventions.java.formatter" to "google", "palantir" or "none" in nitpicker.config.json.
palantir-java-format
A Java file is not formatted with palantir-java-format.
The Java presets keep one layout, the formatter's. palantir-java-format runs in check mode and reports every file it would change.

File is not formatted with palantir-java-format. Run nitpicker --fix, or format it with palantir-java-format --palantir --replace <Java files>. Not your formatter: pin "conventions.java.formatter" to "google", "palantir" or "none" in nitpicker.config.json.
pmd
An inline suppression of pmd in a Java source.

Do not silence PMD inline: fix the finding. PMD also honors "all", "unused", "serial" and "fallthrough". The one accepted marker is @SuppressWarnings("PMD.SpringDataNativeQuery") on a repository method that needs native SQL.
spotbugs
An inline suppression of spotbugs in a Java source.
Do not silence SpotBugs inline: fix the bug.
spring
active-profile
`spring.profiles.active` or `spring.profiles.include` with a literal value in the main (profile-less) document, one finding per line.

Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.

values.label: spring.profiles.active
values.message: Set SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE in each deployment instead, or spring.profiles.default for a fallback that a deployment can override. spring.profiles.active in the packaged main file turns those profiles on in every environment.

values.label: spring.profiles.include
values.message: Name them in a spring.profiles.group entry instead, and activate that group with SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE in each deployment. spring.profiles.include in the packaged main file turns those profiles on in every environment.

values: actuator-exposure

`management.endpoints.web.exposure.include` containing `*` or a sensitive endpoint (below); `management.endpoints.access.default=unrestricted`; `management.endpoint.shutdown.access=unrestricted`; `management.endpoint.heapdump.access` `read-only` or `unrestricted`; `management.endpoint.shutdown.enabled` or `management.endpoints.enabled-by-default` true.

values.label: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include
values.message: List only the actuator endpoints you need in management.endpoints.web.exposure.include, for example health,info; * exposes every endpoint.

values.label: management.endpoints.access.default
values.message: Leave management.endpoints.access.default unset, or set it to read-only, and open single endpoints with management.endpoint.<id>.access; unrestricted also opens the shutdown and heapdump endpoints.

values.label: management.endpoint.heapdump.access
values.message: Set management.endpoint.heapdump.access to none, or remove it; unrestricted lets callers stop the application or download its memory.

values.label: management.endpoint.shutdown.enabled
values.message: Remove management.endpoint.shutdown.enabled=true; it turns the shutdown endpoint on.

values: ddl-auto
`spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto` or `spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto` other than `none`/`validate`, or `spring.jpa.generate-ddl` true.

values.label: spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto
values.message: Manage the schema with Flyway or Liquibase and set spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto to none or validate; other modes let Hibernate change the schema.

values.label: spring.jpa.generate-ddl
values.message: Manage the schema with Flyway or Liquibase and keep spring.jpa.generate-ddl false; true lets Hibernate change the schema.

values: error-details
`server.error.include-stacktrace`, `include-message` or `include-binding-errors` set to `always` or `on-param`; `include-exception` true; also as a placeholder default (`${X:always}`).

values.label: server.error.include-stacktrace
values.message: Set server.error.include-stacktrace=never; other values send stack traces to clients.

values.label: server.error.include-message
values.message: Set server.error.include-message=never and return a fixed ProblemDetail from a @RestControllerAdvice; other values send exception messages to clients.

values.label: server.error.include-binding-errors
values.message: Set server.error.include-binding-errors=never and report field errors from a @RestControllerAdvice; other values send rejected values to clients.

values.label: server.error.include-exception
values.message: Set server.error.include-exception=false; true sends exception class names to clients.

values: literal-secret
A literal value under a key whose last segment is, or ends in a separate word that is, a secret word (below).

values.label: spring.datasource.password
values.message: Set SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD in the environment, or read it from a secret store, and remove the literal secret from spring.datasource.password.

values.label: spring.datasource.url
values.message: Supply the credential in spring.datasource.url from the environment, for example through a placeholder without a default, and take it out of the URL.

values: missing-enable

`@Scheduled`, `@Async`, the cache annotations, `@PreAuthorize` and friends, or `@Retryable` used in Java or Kotlin while no main class has the matching `@Enable...` and no XML `annotation-driven` element enables it.

values.label: enable-scheduling
values.message: Add @EnableScheduling to one @Configuration class; without it @Scheduled does nothing.

values: open-in-view
JPA in the main sources (`jakarta.persistence` or `javax.persistence` import) and `spring.jpa.open-in-view` unset, or true.

values.label: spring.jpa.open-in-view
values.message: Set spring.jpa.open-in-view=false. Spring Boot enables open-in-view by default, which holds a database connection through view rendering and hides N+1 queries.

values: risky-startup-flags
`spring.main.allow-circular-references`, `allow-bean-definition-overriding` or `lazy-initialization` true.

values.label: spring.main.allow-circular-references
values.message: Remove spring.main.allow-circular-references=true and restructure the beans; the flag hides wiring problems instead of fixing them.

values: unsafe-diagnostics

`spring.jpa.show-sql` or `spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.show_sql` true; Hibernate bind logging (`org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind`, `orm.jdbc.extract`, `type.descriptor.sql`, any parent such as `org.hibernate.type`, and `root`) at TRACE or ALL; `management.endpoint.env.show-values`, `configprops.show-values`, `health.show-details` or `health.show-components` `always`; `spring.h2.console.enabled` or `settings.web-allow-others` true; also as a placeholder default (`${SHOW_SQL:true}`).

values.label: spring.jpa.show-sql
values.message: Log SQL with the logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL logger in a local profile and remove spring.jpa.show-sql=true, which prints SQL to standard output, outside logging.

values.label: logging.level.org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind
values.message: Leave logging.level.org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind at its default level; trace logs bound SQL values, including passwords and personal data.

values.label: spring.h2.console.enabled
values.message: Enable spring.h2.console.enabled only in a local profile; it opens the H2 web console.

values.label: management.endpoint.env.show-values
values.message: Set management.endpoint.env.show-values to when-authorized or never; always serves internals to every caller.

values: test-runtime
test-not-run
A test class that no Test task or Failsafe execution runs.
A test that never runs cannot fail, so it proves nothing.

values.label: Gradle
values.message: Register a Test task for the <sourceSet> source set (testClassesDirs = sourceSets.<sourceSet>.output.classesDirs, classpath = sourceSets.<sourceSet>.runtimeClasspath) so <Test> runs: no test task runs that source set, so its tests never run.

values.label: Maven
values.message: Bind the integration-test and verify goals of maven-failsafe-plugin in this module so <Test>IT runs: Surefire skips classes named IT*, *IT and *ITCase, and Failsafe does not run here, so its tests never run.
